items.name: sweep-max-seq
items.recover: cd ~/git/deepseek-v41-flash-spark && ./stop.sh >/dev/null 2>&1; sleep 4; DSV41_CB3_CACHE=$HOME/dsv41-cb3/experts-cb3-s3.bin DSV41_DENSE_FP4=attn,wo_a DSV41_HEAD_FMT=fp8 ./start.sh --no-wait >/dev/null 2>&1; for i in $(seq 1 25); do curl -sf -m 3 http://127.0.0.1:8001/health >/dev/null && break; sleep 15; done
items.note: vLLM PR #56686 observation 1: the sparse-attention indexer does work proportional to the CONTEXT LIMIT, not the batch's context. Ours does the same -- fastdecode.py:288 scores max_seq//r+1 = 16,385 columns and masks afterwards, against ~31 live on the bench prompt. If decode at 4096 beats 32768 on the same short workload, the width is costing us and by how much. No kernel change needed to find out.

items.note: THIRD attempt. Every counter resets per request, so neither dividing totals by decode steps nor differencing two requests can isolate decode -- prefill dominates and its run-to-run noise swamped the signal, twice. The engine now snapshots at the prefill/decode boundary and exports decode_only; this reads that.

items.name: prefill-reuse-probe
items.note: the two-chunk/one-layer diagnostic that decides the layer-major CED transpose, without rewriting execution order. Arm A re-unpacks the population per chunk as moe_forward_prefill does today; arm B unpacks once and reuses. Isolates the UNPACK half on resident experts -- a floor, since the NVMe half (341 GB re-read on an 11.3k prompt) is larger and not in it.

items.name: sweep-prefill-chunk
items.note: prefill is 79% of a realistic agent turn and costs 30 MB of NVMe per prompt token. env.example says the miss term is chunks x layers x 7 GB, so quadrupling the chunk should quarter it. Highest-value knob we have not touched.

items.note: NEEDS the probe extended first: arm B must keep 32-expert batching over slices of a pre-unpacked arena, so that 'stop re-unpacking' is separated from 'abandon batching'. The first probe conflated them and arm B lost 33%, probably to cold reads rather than to reuse itself.
